key_insight: Short warm-up training with random noise applied after standard initialization reduces neural network overconfidence by reconfiguring early activations, leading to better uncertainty calibration and improved recognition of unknown (out‑of‑distribution) inputs.
problem_solved: Deep networks tend to be overconfident—especially on unfamiliar inputs—partly due to typical weight initialization; this work addresses miscalibrated predictive uncertainty and poor meta‑cognitive detection of unknowns.
method: Diagnose overconfidence as an artifact of common initialization and early training dynamics.
Introduce a brief ‘warm‑up’ phase that trains the network on random noise (no labels) immediately after initialization to reshape early activations.
Continue with standard supervised training; evaluate improvements in calibration and OOD recognition compared to baselines.
impact: A simple, low‑cost modification to the training pipeline that significantly improves predictive calibration and out‑of‑distribution detection without changing architectures or loss functions—easy to adopt in practical ML workflows.
visual_elements: Before/after reliability diagrams (calibration curves) showing predicted confidence vs. accuracy
Bar chart or table comparing calibration metrics (ECE, Brier) and OOD detection AUC with and without noise warm‑up
Schematic pipeline: initialization → random‑noise warm‑up (brief) → standard training
Illustration of confidence distributions (histograms) for in‑distribution vs. out‑of‑distribution samples pre/post warm‑up
paper_title: Brain-inspired warm-up training with random noise for uncertainty calibration
